settings.title: Literacy before the jar
settings.text: A customer who understands congestion, barrier stress, and UV load rarely buys the wrong product twice. Education is part of the product.

settings.title: Built for Indian conditions
settings.text: Heat, humidity, hard water, pollution, and year-round UV are not afterthoughts. They shape which actives we choose and how we deliver them.

settings.title: Named doses, named roles
settings.text: When concentration matters, we show it. Every ingredient must earn its place with a mechanism — not a decorative label claim.

settings.title: Comfort is not optional
settings.text: Acne-prone care that abandons the barrier creates a longer problem. Clarity and repair belong in the same sequence.

settings.title: Acne literacy
settings.text: Breakouts are biology meeting climate — not a cleanliness failure.

settings.title: Barrier first
settings.text: When cream fails, the lipid layer is usually the real issue.

settings.title: Daily SPF
settings.text: In India, photoprotection is structural — not a summer accessory.

settings.title: Seasonal modules
settings.text: Monsoon, festive, and winter change the same biology in different ways.

settings.heading: We brought the why back to skincare.
settings.text: Project Skin exists because the industry sold ritual instead of root cause. We sell literacy first, formulations second — for Indian skin, climate, and real routines.
settings.body_text: Skin is an organ, not a canvas. What you apply interacts with biology, barrier lipids, and the environment you live in. Our work starts there — then the formula.
settings.split_heading: Engineered for this climate — not adapted later.
settings.split_text: Global routines often assume mild seasons and soft water. Urban India stacks UV extremes, monsoon humidity, winter TEWL, hard-water cleanses, and pollution in one year. That is the brief we design against.
settings.cards_text: Pick the story that matches what you see on your skin — then decide what to buy.
settings.cta_text: Thirty minutes with a dermatologist — climate, history, and a plan you can keep.
